ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a vacuum, there are three locations P, M, and N. Moving an electron (with charge -e) from point P to point M requires overcoming the electric field force with work done of $20\mathrm{eV}$. Moving the electron from point M to point N results in the electric field force doing work of $30\mathrm{eV}$.

1. Determine the potential difference $U_{PM}$ between points P and M, and the potential difference $U_{MN}$ between points M and N.
2. Assuming the electric potential at point M is zero, calculate the electric potential $\varphi_P$ at point P and the electric potential energy $E_P$ of the electron at point P.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In a vacuum, there are three locations P, M, and N. Moving an electron (with charge -e) from point P to point M requires overcoming the electric field force with work done of $20\mathrm{eV}$. Moving the electron from point M to point N results in the electric field force doing work of $30\mathrm{eV}$. 1. Determine the potential difference $U_{PM}$ between points P and M, and the potential difference $U_{MN}$ between points M and N. 2. Assuming the electric potential at point M is zero, calculate the electric potential $\varphi_P$ at point P and the electric potential energy $E_P$ of the electron at point P.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The attached figure is a simple schematic diagram of a triangle, with the three vertices labeled P, M, and N respectively; P is located above, M is located at the lower left, and N is located at the lower right. The problem discusses the relationship between the work done by the electric field force and the potential difference when an electron moves along the two segments P→M and M→N. Then reason: Adopt the convention U_PM=φ_P−φ_M, U_MN=φ_M−φ_N, and the work done by the electric field force W_field=qU. The electron charge q=−e. When the electron goes from P to M, “overcoming the electric field force to do work 20 eV” indicates that the work done by the electric field force is W_field(P→M)=−20 eV. Therefore −20 eV=(−e)U_PM, giving U_PM=20 V. When the electron goes from M to N, the work done by the electric field force is 30 eV, namely W_field(M→N)=+30 eV, so 30 eV=(−e)U_MN, giving U_MN=−30 V. If φ_M=0, then U_PM=φ_P−φ_M=φ_P, therefore φ_P=20 V. The electric potential energy of the electron at point P is E_P=qφ_P=(−e)(20 V)=−20 eV.
